title: What happened in AI — Sep 21, 2026
intro: Z.ai's data-handling scandal dominated security news today: the coding-assistant vendor disabled features, then open-sourced ZCode with a third-party audit confirming the disputed cloud data was wiped, even as parent Zhipu AI faces scrutiny over the timing next to its 33.5 billion yuan financing round.

Elsewhere, NVIDIA, InfoQ, and OpenAI's own agent-harness talk all converged on treating agent security as ordinary engineering discipline, while China's open-weight labs kept racing each other on benchmarks, licensing, and now retail distribution.
highlights: Z.ai's data-handling scandal escalated all day: coding-assistant features got disabled, then ZCode was open-sourced with a third-party deletion audit and no-retention plans for its MaaS.
NVIDIA, InfoQ, and OpenAI's Vinoth Govindarajan all pushed the same message: production agent security is a control-plane and ownership problem, not a model-capability one.
OpenAI's V7 gives agents institutional memory from a company's own files; Motif Labs open-sourced shared memory for teams of coding agents.
vLLM's disaggregated prefill/decode recipe hit 5K throughput on Qwen3.8-2.4T with GB300 NVL72 — with steps to reproduce it.
Tencent's 770B Hy4 preview and Kimi K3's first Amazon listing both target the same prize: dominance among Chinese open-weight models.

categories.name: Agent Security & Governance Frameworks
categories.summary: Three pieces converged on the same engineering answer to agent security: treat it as ordinary infrastructure work — defined requirements, enforceable controls, named owners, and an explicit control plane — not a model-capability problem.

articles.title: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack
articles.summary: NVIDIA frames agent security as engineering, not a model property: defined requirements, enforceable controls, named owners, and evidence the protections actually work.

articles.title: Presentation: The Agent Harness: Control Planes, Invariants, and Approval Boundaries for Production AI Agents
articles.summary: OpenAI's Vinoth Govindarajan argues production agents fail beyond hallucination, and lays out control planes, invariants, and approval boundaries as the fix, using the OpenClaw incident as a case study.

articles.title: Podcast: Securing AI Agents: Identity, Authorization, and the DPACT Framework
articles.summary: Sahil Agarwal introduces DPACT — Delegation, Policy, Auditability, Context, and Trust — as a framework for identity and authorization in agent systems.

categories.name: Z.ai's Coding-Agent Data Controversy Escalates
categories.summary: A day after Z.ai's unauthorized-upload scandal broke, the fallout hit both product and company: coding-assistant features were disabled, ZCode was open-sourced with a third-party deletion audit, and parent Zhipu AI announced no-retention plans — all while the timing next to its 33.5 billion yuan raise drew scrutiny.

articles.title: Zhipu AI Faces "Unauthorized Data Transmission" Controversy Shortly After Closing 33.5 Billion Yuan Financing Round
articles.summary: A new unauthorized-data-transmission controversy hit Zhipu AI just after it closed a 33.5 billion yuan financing round.

articles.title: ZCode: Z.ai's coding agent harness. Powerful, intelligent, extensible
articles.summary: Z.ai's coding-agent harness, ZCode, is now a public GitHub repo — the same tool at the center of the data-handling dispute.

articles.title: Zhipu open-sources ZCode after data dispute and plans no-retention controls for MaaS
articles.summary: Zhipu open-sourced ZCode in response to the dispute and says it plans no-retention controls for its model-as-a-service offering.

articles.title: Zhipu AI Officially Open-Sources ZCode; Third-Party Audit Confirms Cloud Data Wiped Clean
articles.summary: A third-party audit Zhipu commissioned found the disputed cloud data had been wiped clean, the company said alongside the open-source release.

articles.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
articles.summary: Despite the open-source release and audit, Z.ai went on to disable AI coding-assistant features later the same day over a security issue.

categories.name: Agent Memory, Evals & Coding-Agent Design
categories.summary: Builders are converging on giving agents durable memory and better judgment: shared memory across coding-agent teams, evals scored by a non-LLM judge, and design notes on type safety for coding agents.

articles.title: How V7 gives AI agents institutional memory
articles.summary: Built on GPT-5.6, V7 turns a company's scattered files into a context store agents can pull from to finish complex, source-linked work.

articles.title: Show HN: Open-source shared memory for teams of AI coding agents
articles.summary: Motif Labs open-sourced a shared-memory layer so multiple AI coding agents on the same team can see each other's context.

articles.title: Jev is now available in LangSmith Evals
articles.summary: LangSmith's Jev judge scores agent traces with faster, cheaper structured feedback across production runs, datasets, and regression tests.

articles.title: Diogo Almeida: Thoughts on a Typesafe Coding Agent
articles.summary: A developer's notes argue coding agents need type-safety guarantees built into the harness, not bolted on after generation.

categories.name: AI Infrastructure & Inference
categories.summary: Serving and platform teams got two concrete levers today — a disaggregated prefill/decode recipe for a large MoE model and Python support in Cloudflare's edge runtime — plus a reminder that AI-factory buildouts now hinge on power and cooling procurement, not just chips.

articles.title: PD Serving of Qwen3.8-2.4T
articles.summary: vLLM shows prefill/decode-disaggregated serving hitting 5K throughput and 180 interactivity on Qwen3.8-2.4T using GB300 NVL72, with steps to reproduce the numbers.

articles.title: Python Workers are now generally available
articles.summary: Cloudflare's Python Workers reached GA, letting AI orchestration libraries and Python web frameworks run natively on its edge runtime with direct access to D1, R2, and Workers AI.

articles.title: NVIDIA Launches DSX Ready to Qualify Power and Cooling Products for AI Factories
articles.summary: NVIDIA's new DSX Ready program qualifies power and cooling products for AI-factory buildouts, as site, water, and grid constraints increasingly gate what operators can deploy.

categories.name: Chinese Open-Weight Model Race
categories.summary: China's open-weight labs kept shipping and benchmarking against each other — a research-only open image model, a 770B contender aimed at Kimi K3, and Kimi K3's first retail distribution test — against a backdrop of tightening US export-control workarounds.

articles.title: The current balance of power in open models
articles.summary: Interconnects' expanded congressional testimony lays out where open-weight models currently stand against closed frontier labs.

articles.title: Qwen-Image-2.1 generates transparent images from open weights, but research use only
articles.summary: Alibaba's Qwen-Image-2.1 adds native transparency to open-weight image generation, but ships under a research-only license.

articles.title: Tencent Hy4 Preview Benchmarks: 770B Open Model Takes on Kimi K3
articles.summary: Tencent's 770B-parameter Hy4 preview posts benchmarks aimed squarely at unseating Moonshot's Kimi K3.

articles.title: Moonshot's Kimi K3 lands on Amazon in key test for Chinese open-source AI income
articles.summary: Kimi K3's listing on Amazon is a first real test of whether Chinese open-source labs can convert usage into retail distribution revenue.

articles.title: DeepSeek Expects Huawei Chip Deliveries to Bypass US Export Controls, The Information Reports
articles.summary: DeepSeek reportedly expects its Huawei training-chip deliveries to route around current US export controls, per The Information.

categories.name: AI Governance & Standards
categories.summary: OpenAI made two governance moves today: proposing a path to shared global AI evaluation and reporting standards, and forming an outside advisory group to vet how AI-derived math results get reviewed and communicated.

articles.title: Building standards for the next phase of AI
articles.summary: OpenAI calls for coordinated global evaluation, reporting, and governance standards as AI capability scales.

articles.title: Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence
articles.summary: OpenAI is working with an independent advisory group to guide how emerging AI-derived math results get reviewed and communicated.
